title: Yiddish History Told With His Bear Hug Bent

contact_edits.before: Running just longer than an hour and a half, this is a scattershot entertainment. There are some songs, in excellent English translations by Bikel himself. There are random glimpses of shtetl boyhood, involving a rabbi who would as soon beat a student as teach him and a best friend with a marked resemblance to Huck Finn; indeed, we're told that Sholom Aleichem and Mark Twain regarded one another as kindred spirits. The show only partly lives up to its subtitle. There is laughter, certainly, and there's the occcasional sigh, but the tears have to be taken as read. - Sholom Aleichem continues to Oct. 18. Call 416-872-5555 for ticket information.
